column5: Windows and curtains are watcher places by one rule: a figure behind net curtains sees out at reduced light and is seen only as a twitch, so the player can learn to read them.
column6: Windows and curtains as watcher places

column4: She remembers both: the payment and the beating, which is a new deed where she is a victim and likelier to report.
A firm jacket is a coat like any other and no key to a back room.
column5: Under the dress rule the firm's jacket marks him as one of Mickey's drivers to staff who do not know the drivers' faces, and the back room is open to a driver on a fare.
column6: Dress read against place and role

column4: A figure at a lit window is a watcher and sight follows distance and light, but glass and net curtains have no effect written.
column5: Windows and curtains are watcher places: glass at night lowers what a watcher catches by the street's light, net curtains lower it again and hide the watcher to a twitch.
column6: Windows and curtains as watcher places

column4: A man who belongs at a bus stop draws no second look and a crowd slows a glance, but how a searcher checks faces in a crowd is not written.
column5: Searchers check faces against what they hold: an alert searcher looks at each face in reach in turn, so standing in a queue works against someone holding only a coat and fails against one who knows the face.
column6: Searchers check faces against what they hold

column4: Anyone notices a follower by the tailing rules (look-back every 20 to 40 s, a mark is a doubt), but suspicion over a long stretch from repeated turnings is a listed missing build.
column5: Anyone notices being followed by time in view and repeats: each same turning raises doubt, closeness raises it faster, and doubt shows before he acts.
column6: Tailing and being watched as one rule

column4: A noise draws a watcher to look and he settles in a minute remembering there was a noise; a burglar alarm brings a constable, but growing wise to a second trick is not written.
column5: Watchers learn from what they remember: a second noise of the same kind within the hour makes him search for a person instead of the noise, and he tells others.
column6: Watchers learn from what they remember

column4: A figure at a lit window is a watcher who holds what she saw at its certainty; net curtains are not modelled.
column5: Windows and curtains are watcher places: a neighbour behind net curtains sees at reduced light and shows only as a twitch, and what she holds goes to the street and the constable.
column6: Windows and curtains as watcher places
